name: cf-email-sender
title: Cloudflare Email Service sender with dev printing and a test override
description: mailer(env) over the send_email binding EMAIL, from MAIL_FROM with the app's name; prints instead of sending in dev; null in production when unbound, so callers refuse instead of faking delivery. sendMail() logs only the Email Service error code. An inline-styled HTML layout and escaping helper. A test override captures mail.
author: Coop <coop@xavalabs.com>

params.name: appName
params.description: Sender display name and the heading of the HTML layout.

params.name: appDomain
params.description: Domain of the MAIL_FROM default (login@<appDomain>); it must be onboarded in Email Service.

params.name: mailer
params.description: email-service sends through the EMAIL binding; console only prints (dev), and is null in production.

env.name: MAIL_FROM
env.description: Sender address; its domain must be onboarded in Cloudflare Email Service.

env.name: ENVIRONMENT
env.description: dev, development, local or test print mail instead of failing when EMAIL is unbound; anything else (production) gets no mailer.

bindings.name: EMAIL
bindings.note: Without it mail is printed in dev and mailer(env) is null in production.

agent.summary: Adds a mail module for Workers over Cloudflare Email Service: mailer(env) and sendMail(env, mail), printed in dev, refused in production when unbound, overridable in tests. One send_email binding and one var.
when_to_use: The app sends its own transactional mail (sign-in codes, invitations, receipts) from a Worker.
Another block lists it in registryDependencies (email-code-auth, orgs-roles-invites).
when_not_to_use: Bulk or marketing mail, or tracked campaigns.
A provider other than Cloudflare Email Service is required.

adapt.title: Onboard the sending domain in Email Service
adapt.do: Cloudflare dashboard, Email, Email Service: add {{kit.appDomain}}; keep MAIL_FROM in wrangler.jsonc vars on that domain; set ENVIRONMENT to production in the deployed config.
adapt.check: A mail sent from staging arrives; sendMail does not throw E_SENDER_NOT_VERIFIED.

agent.author_notes: Treat a null mailer as 'feature unavailable' (HTTP 501), never as success.
